correctness.rationale: Somu–Kukla–Tran Lemma 3.3 guarantees sufficiently late minimal consecutive-prime squarefree blocks are Zumkeller; inspecting its exact definition gives 2<=P<8/3 and the Euler product gives phi(Z)/Z>3/pi^2. Arbitrarily many disjoint prime blocks exist. Their pairwise-coprime CRT events have product density <=(1-3/pi^2)^K. For fixed Z and N coprime to Z, reduced class N-Z modulo Z^2 has a prime p<=N/2 for every sufficiently large N by the unconditional fixed-modulus PNT, and N-p=Z(1+Zt) is Zumkeller. Thus exceptional upper density <=(1-3/pi^2)^K for every K and equals zero. The prime-block lemma is an established cited ingredient, not inferred from experiments.

value.rationale: Proves the exact prime-summand zero-density component of named Conjecture 4.21; gives a natural explicit CRT periodic envelope of density at most (1-3/pi^2)^K, clarifies coverage of even integers not implied by existing odd-only quantitative results. It is an infinite density theorem, not a routine restatement of the source prime-block lemma or a finite census.
